functions.title: Plot receptor groups on a tissue image
functions.summary: `plotReceptors` plots the spots that hold receptors.
functions.markdown:
# plotReceptors

## Plot receptor groups on a tissue image

## Description

`plotReceptors` plots the spots that hold receptors. It colors the spots by receptor group, or by a continuous value.

## Usage

``` R
plotReceptors(
  object,
  receptors = NULL,
  group = NULL,
  group_val = NULL,
  spatial_id = NULL,
  colors = NULL,
  overlap = "average",
  value = NULL,
  value_colors = c("#FFFFFF", "#000080"),
  value_limits = c(0, NA),
  value_combine = c("mean", "median", "mode", "max", "min", "sum"),
  receptor_size = 1,
  receptor_alpha = 1,
  title = NULL,
  order_points = TRUE,
  image_scale = NULL,
  swap_coords = NULL,
  images = NULL,
  sample_id = NULL,
  image_alpha = 1,
  zoom = FALSE,
  receptor_legend_title = NULL,
  show_receptor_legend = TRUE,
  polygons = FALSE,
  polygon_x = "x",
  polygon_y = "y",
  polygon_id = "polygon",
  polygon_val = NULL,
  polygon_alpha = 0.2,
  polygon_fill = "#0072B2",
  polygon_color = "#0072B2",
  polygon_linewidth = 0.6,
  polygon_label = FALSE,
  polygon_label_by = NULL,
  polygon_label_size = 3,
  polygon_label_color = "black",
  combine = TRUE,
  combine_sample_plots = FALSE,
  slot = NULL
)
```

## Arguments

`object`

:   Seurat object, or a SIRUP object with spatial data and receptors.

`receptors`

:   AIRR-style receptor table with a spatial ID column and a group column. Omit it if `object` is a SIRUP object.

`group`

:   Name of the `receptors` column that selects and colors the receptor groups, for example `"clone_id"`.

`group_val`

:   Values of `group` to plot. If `NULL`, the function uses all non-missing values.

`spatial_id`

:   Name of the `receptors` column that holds the Seurat spot names. If `NULL`, the function uses the stored field of a SIRUP object, or uses the first standard spatial ID column that it finds.

`colors`

:   Colors of the receptor groups. Named colors match the group values. Unnamed colors follow the order of the values.

`overlap`

:   Color of a spot that holds more than one receptor group. The function draws such a spot once, as a combined group with the member names joined by `" + "`. With `"average"` (default), the spot gets the mean color of its members. With one color, all combined spots get that color.

`value`

:   Color each spot on a continuous gradient and not by group. Give the name of a numeric `receptors` column, or `"count"` for the number of receptors in the spot. You can omit `group` in this mode. If you give it (with `group_val`), the function uses only the matching receptors.

`value_colors`

:   Colors of the `value` gradient (default white to navy). Two colors give a low-to-high gradient. More colors give a gradient with several stops, so you can give a palette such as `viridisLite::viridis(9)`.

`value_limits`

:   Limits of the `value` scale (default `c(0, NA)`, which starts the scale at zero).

`value_combine`

:   How to combine `value` if a spot holds more than one receptor: `"mean"` (default), `"median"`, `"mode"`, `"max"`, `"min"`, or `"sum"`. The function ignores it if `value = "count"`.

`receptor_size`

:   Size of the receptor points (default 1).

`receptor_alpha`

:   Opacity of the receptor points (default 1).

`title`

:   Plot title.

`order_points`

:   Draw the early receptor groups first, so that the later groups show on top (default `TRUE`)?

`image_scale`

:   Image scale for `SeuratObject::GetTissueCoordinates()`. If `NULL`, the function uses the value stored in the SIRUP object.

`swap_coords`

:   Swap the two Seurat coordinate axes? If `NULL`, the function uses the value stored in the SIRUP object. Give a value if `object` is a Seurat object.

`images`

:   Names of the Seurat images to use.

`sample_id`

:   Names of the samples to plot. Use it for multi-sample SIRUP objects. If `NULL`, the function plots all samples.

`image_alpha`

:   Opacity of the tissue image.

`zoom`

:   Zoom to the plotted spots (default `FALSE`)? If `FALSE`, the plot shows the full tissue area that the spatial coordinates cover.

`receptor_legend_title`

:   Title of the receptor legend. If `NULL`, the function uses `group`.

`show_receptor_legend`

:   Show the receptor legend (default `TRUE`)?

`polygons`

:   Draw polygons under the points on each spatial panel. With `FALSE` (default), the function draws no polygons. With `TRUE`, it uses the polygons stored in the SIRUP object. You can also give a data frame of polygon vertices, or the path of a CSV file of polygon vertices. A vertex table needs the columns set by `polygon_x` and `polygon_y`. It needs the column set by `polygon_id` if it holds more than one polygon.

`polygon_x`

:   Name of the x-coordinate column in the polygon table (default `"x"`).

`polygon_y`

:   Name of the y-coordinate column in the polygon table (default `"y"`).

`polygon_id`

:   Name of the column that separates the polygons in the polygon table (default `"polygon"`). If the column does not exist, the function uses a `polygon` or `polygon_id` column. If neither exists, all rows form one polygon.

`polygon_val`

:   IDs of the polygons to draw. If `NULL`, the function draws all polygons.

`polygon_alpha`

:   Opacity of the polygon fill (default 0.2).

`polygon_fill`

:   Fill color of the polygons (default `"#0072B2"`).

`polygon_color`

:   Color of the polygon outlines (default `"#0072B2"`).

`polygon_linewidth`

:   Width of the polygon outlines (default 0.6).

`polygon_label`

:   Write a label at the center of each polygon (default `FALSE`)?

`polygon_label_by`

:   Name of the column that holds the labels. If `NULL`, the function uses the polygon ID.

`polygon_label_size`

:   Text size of the polygon labels (default 3).

`polygon_label_color`

:   Text color of the polygon labels (default `"black"`).

`combine`

:   Combine the image panels with patchwork (default `TRUE`)?

`combine_sample_plots`

:   Combine the plots of all samples into one patchwork (default `FALSE`)? The function uses it only for multi-sample objects. If `FALSE`, it returns a named list with one plot for each sample.

`slot`

:   Name of the receptor slot to use. Leave it `NULL` if the SIRUP object has one receptor table. You must give it if the object has several slots. The function ignores `slot` if you give a plain receptor table.

## Details

#\' If the object has multiple images or samples, the function draws one plot for each image or sample.

## Value

A ggplot object or a patchwork object. If `combine = FALSE`, a list.

## See Also

[`plotReceptorsExpression()`](plotReceptorsExpression.md), [`plotSpatialColorTips()`](plotSpatialColorTips.md)

## Examples

``` R
x <- readSIRUP(system.file("extdata", "sirup_synthetic.rds", package = "SIRUP"))
plotReceptors(x, group = "clone_id")

# Color the spots by the number of receptors in each spot.
plotReceptors(x, value = "count")
```

functions.title: Plot receptor groups over gene expression
functions.summary: `plotReceptorsExpression` plots one feature together with one or more groups of receptors on a tissue image.
functions.markdown:
# plotReceptorsExpression

## Plot receptor groups over gene expression

## Description

`plotReceptorsExpression` plots one feature together with one or more groups of receptors on a tissue image. For example, it shows the BCR-positive and TCR-positive spots on one expression map.

## Usage

``` R
plotReceptorsExpression(
  object,
  receptors = NULL,
  group = NULL,
  group_val = NULL,
  spatial_id = NULL,
  feature = NULL,
  gene = NULL,
  colors = NULL,
  overlap = "average",
  value = NULL,
  value_colors = c("#FFFFFF", "#000080"),
  value_limits = c(0, NA),
  value_combine = c("mean", "median", "mode", "max", "min", "sum"),
  receptor_size = 1,
  receptor_stroke = 0.7,
  receptor_alpha = 1,
  feature_colors = c("#939393", "#FFFF00"),
  feature_size = 1,
  feature_alpha = 1,
  zero_tol = 0,
  title = NULL,
  order_points = TRUE,
  assay = NULL,
  layer = "counts",
  image_scale = NULL,
  swap_coords = NULL,
  images = NULL,
  sample_id = NULL,
  image_alpha = 1,
  zoom = FALSE,
  receptor_legend_title = NULL,
  show_receptor_legend = TRUE,
  combine = TRUE,
  combine_sample_plots = FALSE,
  slot = NULL
)
```

## Arguments

`object`

:   Seurat object, or a SIRUP object with spatial data and receptors.

`receptors`

:   AIRR-style receptor table with a spatial ID column and a group column. Omit it if `object` is a SIRUP object.

`group`

:   Name of the `receptors` column that defines the receptor groups, for example `"receptor_type"` with the values `"BCR"` and `"TCR"`. You can omit it if you give `value`. If you give both, `group` and `group_val` only select the receptors to draw.

`group_val`

:   Group values to plot, in the order of the plot. If `NULL`, the function uses all non-missing values of `group`.

`spatial_id`

:   Name of the `receptors` column that holds the Seurat spot names. If `NULL`, the function uses the stored field of a SIRUP object, or looks for a standard spatial ID column.

`feature`

:   Feature to plot under the spots with receptors.

`gene`

:   Alias for `feature`.

`colors`

:   Colors of the receptor groups. Named colors match the group values. Unnamed colors follow the order of the values.

`overlap`

:   Color of a spot that holds more than one receptor group. The function draws such a spot once, as a combined group with the member names joined by `" + "`. With `"average"` (default), the spot gets the mean color of its members. With one color, all combined spots get that color.

`value`

:   Color the receptor spots on a continuous gradient and not by group. Give the name of a numeric `receptors` column, or `"count"` for the number of receptors in the spot.

`value_colors`

:   Colors of the `value` gradient (default white to navy). Two colors give a low-to-high gradient. More colors give a gradient with several stops.

`value_limits`

:   Limits of the `value` scale (default `c(0, NA)`).

`value_combine`

:   How to combine `value` if a spot holds more than one receptor: `"mean"` (default), `"median"`, `"mode"`, `"max"`, `"min"`, or `"sum"`. The function ignores it if `value = "count"`.

`receptor_size`

:   Size of the receptor circles (default 1).

`receptor_stroke`

:   Line width of the receptor circles (default 0.7).

`receptor_alpha`

:   Opacity of the receptor circles (default 1).

`feature_colors`

:   Colors that make the expression scale (default `c("#939393", "#FFFF00")`).

`feature_size`

:   Size of the expression points (default 1).

`feature_alpha`

:   Opacity of the expression points (default 1).

`zero_tol`

:   Values at or below this threshold count as zero (default 0).

`title`

:   Plot title.

`order_points`

:   Draw the low expression values first, so that the high values show on top (default `TRUE`)? The function draws the receptor groups in the order of `group_val`.

`assay`

:   Assay to use.

`layer`

:   Seurat expression layer to use (default `"counts"`).

`image_scale`

:   Image scale for `SeuratObject::GetTissueCoordinates()`.

`swap_coords`

:   Swap the two Seurat coordinate axes?

`images`

:   Names of the Seurat images to use.

`sample_id`

:   Names of the samples to plot. Use it for multi-sample SIRUP objects. If `NULL`, the function plots all samples.

`image_alpha`

:   Opacity of the tissue image.

`zoom`

:   Zoom to the plotted spots (default `FALSE`)? If `FALSE`, the plot shows the full tissue area that the spatial coordinates cover.

`receptor_legend_title`

:   Title of the receptor legend. If `NULL`, the function uses `group`.

`show_receptor_legend`

:   Show the receptor legend (default `TRUE`)?

`combine`

:   Combine the image panels with patchwork (default `TRUE`)?

`combine_sample_plots`

:   Combine the plots of all samples into one patchwork (default `FALSE`)? The function uses it only for multi-sample objects. If `FALSE`, it returns a named list with one plot for each sample.

`slot`

:   Name of the receptor slot to use. Leave it `NULL` if the SIRUP object has one receptor table. You must give it if the object has several slots. The function ignores `slot` if you give a plain receptor table.

## Details

The function draws the spots with expression above zero with a continuous fill scale. It draws the spots with receptors on top as hollow circles.

If the object has multiple images or samples, the function draws one plot for each image or sample.

## Value

A ggplot object or a patchwork object. If `combine = FALSE`, a list.

## See Also

[`plotReceptors()`](plotReceptors.md), [`spatialExpressionPlot()`](spatialExpressionPlot.md)

## Examples

``` R
x <- readSIRUP(system.file("extdata", "sirup_synthetic.rds", package = "SIRUP"))
plotReceptorsExpression(x, group = "clone_id", feature = "gene1")
```

functions.title: Plot Ripley's cross K against distance
functions.summary: `plotRipleyCrossK` plots the observed cross K, with the simulation envelope if there is one.
functions.markdown:
# plotRipleyCrossK

## Plot Ripley\'s cross K against distance

## Description

`plotRipleyCrossK` plots the observed cross K, with the simulation envelope if there is one.

## Usage

``` R
plotRipleyCrossK(
  kcross,
  title = NULL,
  observed_color = "black",
  simulated_color = "grey30",
  envelope_fill = "grey75",
  envelope_alpha = 0.45,
  facet = TRUE,
  log_y = FALSE
)
```

## Arguments

`kcross`

:   Result of [`spatialRipleyCrossK()`](spatialRipleyCrossK.md).

`title`

:   Plot title.

`observed_color`

:   Color of the observed curve.

`simulated_color`

:   Color of the dotted simulated curve.

`envelope_fill`

:   Fill color of the simulation envelope.

`envelope_alpha`

:   Opacity of the simulation envelope.

`facet`

:   Make one panel for each image if the result has several images (default `TRUE`)?

`log_y`

:   Use a log10 scale for the y-axis (default `FALSE`)?

## Value

A ggplot object.

## See Also

[`spatialRipleyCrossK()`](spatialRipleyCrossK.md)

## Examples

``` R

x <- readSIRUP(system.file("extdata", "sirup_synthetic.rds", package = "SIRUP"))
set.seed(1)
kcross <- spatialRipleyCrossK(
  x,
  mark_col = "cell_type",
  i = "A",
  j = "B",
  nsim = 19
)
plotRipleyCrossK(kcross)
```

functions.title: Plot the tip colors of one clone on a tissue image
functions.summary: `plotSpatialCloneColorTips` plots the spots of one clone.
functions.markdown:
# plotSpatialCloneColorTips

## Plot the tip colors of one clone on a tissue image

## Description

`plotSpatialCloneColorTips` plots the spots of one clone. Each spot gets the color of its tip. The function calls [`plotSpatialColorTips()`](plotSpatialColorTips.md).

## Usage

``` R
plotSpatialCloneColorTips(
  colored_clones,
  clone_val,
  tissue_positions = NULL,
  clone = "clone_id",
  spatial_id = "spatial_id_8um",
  image_scale = NULL,
  swap_coords = NULL,
  sample_id = NULL,
  slot = NULL,
  ...
)
```

## Arguments

`colored_clones`

:   Result of [`assignTipColors()`](assignTipColors.md), or a SIRUP object whose receptor table has the tip colors.

`clone_val`

:   ID of the clone to plot.

`tissue_positions`

:   Seurat object or SIRUP object. Omit it if `colored_clones` is a SIRUP object.

`clone`

:   Name of the column that holds the clone IDs (default `"clone_id"`). If `colored_clones` is a SIRUP object and you omit this argument, the function uses the stored clone field.

`spatial_id`

:   Name of the column in `colored_clones` that holds the spatial IDs (default `"spatial_id_8um"`). If `colored_clones` is a SIRUP object and you omit this argument, the function uses the stored spatial ID field.

`image_scale`

:   Image scale for `SeuratObject::GetTissueCoordinates()`. If `NULL`, the function uses the value stored in the SIRUP object.

`swap_coords`

:   Swap the two Seurat coordinate axes? If `NULL`, the function uses the value stored in the SIRUP object.

`sample_id`

:   Names of the samples to plot. Use it for multi-sample SIRUP objects. If `NULL`, the function plots all samples.

`slot`

:   Name of the receptor slot to use. Leave it `NULL` if the SIRUP object has one receptor table. You must give it if the object has several slots. The function ignores `slot` if you give a plain receptor table.

`...`

:   Other arguments for [`plotSpatialColorTips()`](plotSpatialColorTips.md).

## Value

A ggplot object.

## See Also

[`plotSpatialColorTips()`](plotSpatialColorTips.md), [`assignTipColors()`](assignTipColors.md), [`plotSpatialCloneTreePairs()`](plotSpatialCloneTreePairs.md)

## Examples

``` R
x <- readSIRUP(system.file("extdata", "sirup_synthetic.rds", package = "SIRUP"))
x <- updateReceptors(x, assignTipColors, shared_color = "spatial_id")
plotSpatialCloneColorTips(x, clone_val = "1")
```

functions.title: Plot 3D clone-density surfaces on a tissue image
functions.summary: `plotSpatialCloneDensity3D` draws a smoothed density surface for each clone above the tissue image in an interactive rgl scene.
functions.markdown:
# plotSpatialCloneDensity3D

## Plot 3D clone-density surfaces on a tissue image

## Description

`plotSpatialCloneDensity3D` draws a smoothed density surface for each clone above the tissue image in an interactive rgl scene.

## Usage

``` R
plotSpatialCloneDensity3D(
  dominance,
  object,
  clone = "clone_id",
  weight = NULL,
  images = NULL,
  sample_id = NULL,
  image_scale = NULL,
  swap_coords = NULL,
  polygon_val = NULL,
  top_n = 10,
  other_label = "Other",
  other_color = "#D3D3D3",
  plot_other = TRUE,
  bandwidth = NULL,
  grid_n = 80,
  plot_type = c("density", "histogram"),
  hist_bins = 30,
  zoom = FALSE,
  height_scale = 0.22,
  z_offset = 0.04,
  density_alpha = 0.55,
  density_floor = 0.03,
  image_alpha = 1,
  show_points = FALSE,
  point_size = 5,
  point_alpha = 0.75,
  show_polygon = TRUE,
  polygon_color = "white",
  polygon_lwd = 3,
  label_density_peaks = FALSE,
  label_top_n = 5,
  label_cex = 0.8,
  show_axes = TRUE,
  texture_dir = NULL,
  as_widget = TRUE,
  return_data = FALSE
)
```

## Arguments

`dominance`

:   Result of [`spatialCloneDominance()`](spatialCloneDominance.md).

`object`

:   Seurat object or SIRUP object.

`clone`

:   Name of the column in `dominance$region_receptors` that defines the clone groups. If you omit it, the function uses the clone column that [`spatialCloneDominance()`](spatialCloneDominance.md) recorded (default `"clone_id"`).

`weight`

:   Name of a numeric column that gives the weight of each receptor. If `NULL`, each receptor row counts as one.

`images`

:   Names of the Seurat images to use.

`sample_id`

:   Names of the samples to plot. Use it for multi-sample SIRUP objects. If `NULL`, the function plots all samples.

`image_scale`

:   Image scale for `SeuratObject::GetTissueCoordinates()`. If `NULL`, the function uses the value stored in the SIRUP object.

`swap_coords`

:   Swap the two Seurat coordinate axes? If `NULL`, the function uses the value stored in the SIRUP object. Give a value if `object` is a Seurat object.

`polygon_val`

:   IDs of the polygons to select from `dominance`.

`top_n`

:   Number of the most abundant clone groups to show on their own (default 10). The function groups the other clone groups under `other_label`.

`other_label`

:   Label for the grouped clone groups (default `"Other"`).

`other_color`

:   Color of the grouped clone groups (default `"#D3D3D3"`).

`plot_other`

:   Plot the grouped clone groups (default `TRUE`)?

`bandwidth`

:   Bandwidth of the Gaussian kernel, in coordinate units. Give one value for equal smoothing in x and y, or two values (x, y). If `NULL`, the function estimates it from the coordinates in the regions.

`grid_n`

:   Number of grid points for the density surfaces (default 80). Give one value for both axes, or two values (x, y).

`plot_type`

:   Type of plot: `density` (smoothed surfaces) or `histogram` (binned 3D bars).

`hist_bins`

:   Number of x and y bins, if `plot_type = "histogram"` (default 30).

`zoom`

:   Zoom the image plane and the 3D view to the selected region (default `FALSE`)? If `FALSE`, the plot shows the full image.

`height_scale`

:   Maximum height of the density, as a fraction of the plotted range (default 0.22).

`z_offset`

:   Vertical gap between the density surfaces and the tissue image, as a fraction of the plotted range (default 0.04).

`density_alpha`

:   Opacity of the density surfaces (default 0.55).

`density_floor`

:   Relative density below which the function hides surface cells (default 0.03). This removes the low Gaussian tails, which can look like a colored plane.

`image_alpha`

:   Opacity of the tissue image plane.

`show_points`

:   Show the receptor locations above the tissue plane (default `FALSE`)?

`point_size`

:   Size of the receptor points (default 5).

`point_alpha`

:   Opacity of the receptor points (default 0.75).

`show_polygon`

:   Show the polygon boundaries above the tissue plane (default `TRUE`)?

`polygon_color`

:   Color of the polygon boundary lines (default `"white"`).

`polygon_lwd`

:   Width of the polygon boundary lines (default 3).

`label_density_peaks`

:   Label the highest point of the first density surfaces (default `FALSE`)?

`label_top_n`

:   Number of surfaces to label, if `label_density_peaks` is `TRUE` (default 5).

`label_cex`

:   Text scale of the peak labels (default 0.8).

`show_axes`

:   Show the 3D bounding box and the axis labels (default `TRUE`)?

`texture_dir`

:   Directory to write the tissue texture PNG file to. Use a permanent directory if you save an HTML widget.

`as_widget`

:   Return an rgl htmlwidget (default `TRUE`)? If `FALSE`, the function draws the scene and returns the ID of the current rgl device.

`return_data`

:   Return the density data and do not draw the scene (default `FALSE`)? This does not need `rgl`.

## Details

The function uses the receptor rows in the result of [`spatialCloneDominance()`](spatialCloneDominance.md). It needs the `rgl` package, except if you set `return_data = TRUE`.

## Value

An rgl widget or an rgl device ID. If `return_data = TRUE`, a list of the plot data.

## See Also

[`spatialCloneDominance()`](spatialCloneDominance.md), [`plotSpatialRegionReceptors()`](plotSpatialRegionReceptors.md)

## Examples

``` R
x <- readSIRUP(system.file("extdata", "sirup_synthetic.rds", package = "SIRUP"))
dominance <- spatialCloneDominance(x)

# Return the density data. This needs no rgl window.
density <- plotSpatialCloneDensity3D(dominance, x, return_data = TRUE)
names(density)
```

functions.title: Plot a clone join-count result
functions.summary: `plotSpatialCloneJoinCount` plots the tissue map of one tested clone.
functions.markdown:
# plotSpatialCloneJoinCount

## Plot a clone join-count result

## Description

`plotSpatialCloneJoinCount` plots the tissue map of one tested clone. It also shows the observed and expected number of joins between spots of the same clone.

## Usage

``` R
plotSpatialCloneJoinCount(
  join_count,
  object,
  clone_val,
  images = NULL,
  sample_id = NULL,
  polygon_val = NULL,
  polygon = NULL,
  image_scale = NULL,
  swap_coords = NULL,
  show_neighbors = TRUE,
  clone_color = "#D55E00",
  other_color = "grey75",
  point_size = 1.8,
  point_alpha = 0.9,
  edge_width = 0.6,
  edge_alpha = 0.75,
  polygon_color = "black",
  polygon_linewidth = 0.6,
  image_alpha = 1,
  zoom = FALSE,
  title = NULL,
  combine_sample_plots = FALSE
)
```

## Arguments

`join_count`

:   Result of [`spatialCloneJoinCount()`](spatialCloneJoinCount.md). Run that function with `return_data = TRUE`.

`object`

:   Seurat object with spatial images, or a SIRUP object.

`clone_val`

:   Clone ID to plot.

`images`

:   Names of the images to plot.

`sample_id`

:   Names of the samples to plot. Use it for multi-sample SIRUP objects. If `NULL`, the function plots all samples.

`polygon_val`

:   IDs of the polygons to include.

`polygon`

:   Data frame of polygon vertices to draw on the tissue.

`image_scale`

:   Image scale for `SeuratObject::GetTissueCoordinates()`. If `NULL`, the function uses the value stored in the SIRUP object.

`swap_coords`

:   Swap the two Seurat coordinate axes? If `NULL`, the function uses the value stored in the SIRUP object.

`show_neighbors`

:   Draw a line between each pair of neighboring spots that both contain the clone (default `TRUE`)?

`clone_color`

:   Color of the spots and lines for the clone.

`other_color`

:   Color of the other spots that have receptors.

`point_size`

:   Size of the spots.

`point_alpha`

:   Opacity of the spots.

`edge_width`

:   Width of the neighbor lines.

`edge_alpha`

:   Opacity of the neighbor lines.

`polygon_color`

:   Color of the polygon outlines.

`polygon_linewidth`

:   Width of the polygon outlines.

`image_alpha`

:   Opacity of the tissue image.

`zoom`

:   Zoom to the spots in the test (default `FALSE`)?

`title`

:   Title of the combined plot.

`combine_sample_plots`

:   Combine the plots of all samples into one figure (default `FALSE`)? The function uses it only for multi-sample objects. If `FALSE`, it returns a named list with one plot for each sample.

## Details

The map uses the same spots and the same neighbor graph as the call to [`spatialCloneJoinCount()`](spatialCloneJoinCount.md).

If the data come from more than one image, or a sirup object with multiple samples, then the function builds a list of plots, one for each sample or image.

## Value

A ggplot object. For a multi-sample object and `combine_sample_plots = FALSE`, a named list of plots.

## See Also

[`spatialCloneJoinCount()`](spatialCloneJoinCount.md)

## Examples

``` R
x <- readSIRUP(system.file("extdata", "sirup_synthetic.rds", package = "SIRUP"))
join_count <- spatialCloneJoinCount(
  x,
  use_stored_polygons = FALSE,
  k = 4,
  return_data = TRUE
)
plotSpatialCloneJoinCount(join_count, x, clone_val = "2")
```

functions.title: Plot each clone tree next to its tissue map
functions.summary: `plotSpatialCloneTreePairs` makes two plots for each clone: the lineage tree, and a tissue map of the tips.
functions.markdown:
# plotSpatialCloneTreePairs

## Plot each clone tree next to its tissue map

## Description

`plotSpatialCloneTreePairs` makes two plots for each clone: the lineage tree, and a tissue map of the tips. Each tip has one color in both plots, so you can find a tip of the tree on the tissue.

## Usage

``` R
plotSpatialCloneTreePairs(
  trees,
  object,
  spatial_id = NULL,
  clone_val = NULL,
  id = "sequence_id",
  sequence_id = id,
  clone = "clone_id",
  color_by = "identity",
  palette = NULL,
  image_scale = NULL,
  swap_coords = NULL,
  images = NULL,
  sample_id = NULL,
  zoom = FALSE,
  tipsize = NULL,
  scale = 0.01,
  layout = "rectangular",
  title = TRUE,
  shape_by = ".sirup_spatial_status",
  shape_values = c(spatial = 21, not_spatial = 22),
  tree_layout = NULL,
  tree_tip_size = NULL,
  tree_linewidth = 0.5,
  tip_stroke = 0.3,
  treescale_fontsize = 3.88,
  treescale = NULL,
  treescale_position = c("bottomleft", "topleft", "midleft"),
  spatial_tip_size = 1.6,
  spatial_tip_alpha = 1,
  order_points = FALSE,
  show_spatial_legend = FALSE,
  combine_sample_plots = FALSE,
  polygons = FALSE,
  polygon_x = "x",
  polygon_y = "y",
  polygon_id = "polygon",
  polygon_val = NULL,
  polygon_alpha = 0.2,
  polygon_fill = "#0072B2",
  polygon_color = "#0072B2",
  polygon_linewidth = 0.6,
  polygon_label = FALSE,
  polygon_label_by = NULL,
  polygon_label_size = 3,
  polygon_label_color = "black",
  nproc = 1L,
  slot = NULL,
  ...
)
```

## Arguments

`trees`

:   Result of [`dowser::getTrees()`](https://dowser.readthedocs.io/en/latest/topics/getTrees/), or a list with an element `trees` that holds this result.

`object`

:   Seurat object or SIRUP object.

`spatial_id`

:   Name of the column in the dowser clone data that holds the Seurat spot names. Omit it if `object` is a SIRUP object.

`clone_val`

:   IDs of the clones to plot. If `NULL`, the function plots all clones.

`id`

:   Name of the column in the dowser clone data that matches the tree tip labels (default `"sequence_id"`).

`sequence_id`

:   Name of the column in the receptor table of `object` that decides which tree tips belong to the current spatial object (default: the value of `id`). The function uses it only if `object` is a SIRUP object. A tip that is not in this column stays in the tree plot, but the map does not show it.

`clone`

:   Name of the column that holds the clone IDs (default `"clone_id"`).

`color_by`

:   Column that sets the colors of the tips in both plots. With `"identity"` (default), each tip gets its own color. With another column, such as `"tree_cluster"` or a spatial ID column, tips that share a value get one color.

`palette`

:   Colors to use. If you give fewer colors than the function needs, it makes more colors by averaging the colors that you give.

`image_scale`

:   Image scale for `SeuratObject::GetTissueCoordinates()`. If `NULL`, the function uses the value stored in the SIRUP object.

`swap_coords`

:   Swap the two Seurat coordinate axes? If `NULL`, the function uses the value stored in the SIRUP object. Give a value if `object` is a Seurat object.

`images`

:   Names of the Seurat images to use.

`sample_id`

:   Names of the samples to plot. Use it for multi-sample SIRUP objects. If `NULL`, the function plots all samples.

`zoom`

:   Zoom the maps to the clone (default `FALSE`)? If `FALSE`, the maps show the full tissue area that the spatial coordinates cover.

`tipsize`

:   Size of the tip points of the tree.

`scale`

:   Distance that the scale bar of the tree shows, in mutations for each site (default 0.01).

`layout`

:   Layout of the tree, for `ggtree::ggtree()` (default `"rectangular"`).

`title`

:   Title of each tree plot. With `TRUE` (default), the title is the clone ID. Give a character string to use it as the title.

`shape_by`

:   Name of the column in the dowser clone data that sets the shape of the tree tips. The default marks a tip as `"spatial"` if it has a spatial ID, and as `"not_spatial"` if it has none.

`shape_values`

:   Named vector of shapes, for [`ggplot2::scale_shape_manual()`](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/reference/scale_shape_manual.html) (default `c(spatial = 21, not_spatial = 22)`). Shapes 21 to 25 are filled shapes: the tip color fills the shape, and the outline is black. Other shapes get the tip color on the whole mark.

`tree_layout`

:   Alias for `layout`.

`tree_tip_size`

:   Alias for `tipsize`.

`tree_linewidth`

:   Line width of the tree branches, for `ggtree::ggtree()` (default 0.5).

`tip_stroke`

:   Outline width of the filled tree tips (default 0.3).

`treescale_fontsize`

:   Font size of the label of the scale bar (default 3.88).

`treescale`

:   Alias for `scale`.

`treescale_position`

:   Position of the scale bar: `"bottomleft"` (default), `"topleft"` (near the root, at the top of the tips), or `"midleft"` (near the root, halfway down the tips).

`spatial_tip_size`

:   Size of the tip points on the map (default 1.6).

`spatial_tip_alpha`

:   Opacity of the tip points on the map (default 1).

`order_points`

:   Draw the early color groups first on the map, so that the later groups show on top (default `FALSE`)?

`show_spatial_legend`

:   Show a color legend below the map, based on the tip colors of the tree (default `FALSE`)?

`combine_sample_plots`

:   Combine the maps of all samples into one patchwork (default `FALSE`)? The function uses it only for multi-sample objects. If `FALSE`, it returns one tree and map pair for each sample.

`polygons`

:   Draw polygons under the points on each spatial panel. With `FALSE` (default), the function draws no polygons. With `TRUE`, it uses the polygons stored in the SIRUP object. You can also give a data frame of polygon vertices, or the path of a CSV file of polygon vertices. A vertex table needs the columns set by `polygon_x` and `polygon_y`. It needs the column set by `polygon_id` if it holds more than one polygon.

`polygon_x`

:   Name of the x-coordinate column in the polygon table (default `"x"`).

`polygon_y`

:   Name of the y-coordinate column in the polygon table (default `"y"`).

`polygon_id`

:   Name of the column that separates the polygons in the polygon table (default `"polygon"`). If the column does not exist, the function uses a `polygon` or `polygon_id` column. If neither exists, all rows form one polygon.

`polygon_val`

:   IDs of the polygons to draw. If `NULL`, the function draws all polygons.

`polygon_alpha`

:   Opacity of the polygon fill (default 0.2).

`polygon_fill`

:   Fill color of the polygons (default `"#0072B2"`).

`polygon_color`

:   Color of the polygon outlines (default `"#0072B2"`).

`polygon_linewidth`

:   Width of the polygon outlines (default 0.6).

`polygon_label`

:   Write a label at the center of each polygon (default `FALSE`)?

`polygon_label_by`

:   Name of the column that holds the labels. If `NULL`, the function uses the polygon ID.

`polygon_label_size`

:   Text size of the polygon labels (default 3).

`polygon_label_color`

:   Text color of the polygon labels (default `"black"`).

`nproc`

:   Number of processes for building the plot pairs (default 1).

`slot`

:   Name of the receptor slot to use. Leave it `NULL` if the SIRUP object has one receptor table. You must give it if the object has several slots. The function ignores `slot` if you give a plain receptor table.

`...`

:   Other arguments for [`plotSpatialColorTips()`](plotSpatialColorTips.md).

## Details

A tip with no spatial ID, or with a spatial ID that is not in `object`, shows in the tree plot only. The map shows only the tips whose spatial ID matches a spot in `object`. In the tree, by default tips with a spot are circles, and tips without a spot are squares.

If the object has multiple images or samples, the function draws one paired plot for each image or sample.

To match the tips to receptors, see [`formatSpatialClones()`](formatSpatialClones.md).

## Value

A named list with one element for each clone. Each element is a list with the items `tree` and `spatial_clone` (the two plots), and `legend` and `legend_rel_height` (for the optional legend).

## See Also

[`spatialCloneTreePairsToPDF()`](spatialCloneTreePairsToPDF.md), [`clusterTreesTips()`](clusterTreesTips.md), [`getSpatialTrees()`](getSpatialTrees.md), [`plotSpatialColorTips()`](plotSpatialColorTips.md), [`plotSpatialCloneColorTips()`](plotSpatialCloneColorTips.md)

## Examples

``` R
x <- readSIRUP(system.file("extdata", "sirup_synthetic.rds", package = "SIRUP"))
x <- formatSpatialClones(
  x,
  id = "sequence_id",
  germ = "germline_alignment_d_mask",
  traits = "spatial_id"
)
x <- getSpatialTrees(x)
trees <- getAnalysis(x, "trees")

pairs <- plotSpatialCloneTreePairs(trees, x, clone_val = "4")
names(pairs)

# Show the tree and the map side by side.
cowplot::plot_grid(pairs[["4"]]$tree, pairs[["4"]]$spatial_clone)
```

# plotSpatialColorTips

`point_alpha`

`show_legend`

`polygons`

: Draw polygons under the points on each spatial panel. With `FALSE` (default), the function draws no polygons. With `TRUE`, it uses the polygons stored in the SIRUP object. You can also give a data frame of polygon vertices, or the path of a CSV file of polygon vertices. A vertex table needs the columns set by `polygon_x` and `polygon_y`. It needs the column set by `polygon_id` if it holds more than one polygon.

`polygon_x`

: Name of the x-coordinate column in the polygon table (default `"x"`).

`polygon_y`

: Name of the y-coordinate column in the polygon table (default `"y"`).

`polygon_id`

: Name of the column that separates the polygons in the polygon table (default `"polygon"`). If the column does not exist, the function uses a `polygon` or `polygon_id` column. If neither exists, all rows form one polygon.

`polygon_val`

: IDs of the polygons to draw. If `NULL`, the function draws all polygons.

`polygon_alpha`

: Opacity of the polygon fill (default 0.2).

`polygon_fill`

: Fill color of the polygons (default `"#0072B2"`).

`polygon_color`

: Color of the polygon outlines (default `"#0072B2"`).

`polygon_linewidth`

: Width of the polygon outlines (default 0.6).

`polygon_label`

: Write a label at the center of each polygon (default `FALSE`)?

`polygon_label_by`

: Name of the column that holds the labels. If `NULL`, the function uses the polygon ID.

`polygon_label_size`

: Text size of the polygon labels (default 3).

`polygon_label_color`

: Text color of the polygon labels (default `"black"`).

`combine`

: Combine the image panels with patchwork (default `TRUE`)?

`combine_sample_plots`

: Combine the plots of all samples into one patchwork (default `FALSE`)? The function uses it only for multi-sample objects. If `FALSE`, it returns a named list with one plot for each sample.

## Details

If the object has multiple images or samples, the function draws one plot for each image or sample.

## Value

A ggplot object or a patchwork object.

## See Also

[`plotSpatialCloneColorTips()`](plotSpatialCloneColorTips.md), [`plotSpatialCloneTreePairs()`](plotSpatialCloneTreePairs.md), [`assignTipColors()`](assignTipColors.md)

x <- readSIRUP(system.file("extdata", "sirup_synthetic.rds", package = "SIRUP"))

functions.title: Plot clonal dominance results within polygons as pies or bars
functions.summary: `plotSpatialPolygonPies` summarizes one receptor column for each polygon.
functions.markdown:
# plotSpatialPolygonPies

## Plot clonal dominance results within polygons as pies or bars

## Description

`plotSpatialPolygonPies` summarizes one receptor column for each polygon. It plots the result as pie charts or stacked bars.

## Usage

``` R
plotSpatialPolygonPies(
  dominance,
  object,
  fill = "clone_id",
  mode = c("side_by_side", "spatial_clipped", "dominance_only", "stacked_bar"),
  top_n = 10,
  label_top_n = 0,
  other_label = "Other",
  other_color = "#D3D3D3",
  plot_other = TRUE,
  images = NULL,
  sample_id = NULL,
  image_scale = NULL,
  swap_coords = NULL,
  polygon_val = NULL,
  polygon_alpha = 0.2,
  image_alpha = 1,
  pie_alpha = 0.9,
  label_size = 3,
  pies_per_page = 6L,
  pie_order = c("receptors", "polygon"),
  spatial_legend = FALSE,
  zoom = FALSE,
  combine_sample_plots = FALSE
)
```

## Arguments

`dominance`

:   Result of [`spatialCloneDominance()`](spatialCloneDominance.md).

`object`

:   Seurat object or SIRUP object.

`fill`

:   Name of the column in `dominance$region_receptors` to summarize. If you omit it, the function uses the clone column that [`spatialCloneDominance()`](spatialCloneDominance.md) recorded (default `"clone_id"`).

`mode`

:   Plot style: `side_by_side`, `spatial_clipped`, `dominance_only`, or `stacked_bar`. See Details.

`top_n`

:   Number of the most frequent `fill` levels to find in each polygon (default 10). The function shows the union of these levels on their own in all polygons. It groups the other levels under `other_label`.

`label_top_n`

:   Number of levels to label in each polygon (default 0).

`other_label`

:   Label for the grouped levels (default `"Other"`).

`other_color`

:   Color of the grouped levels (default `"#D3D3D3"`).

`plot_other`

:   Plot the grouped levels (default `TRUE`)?

`images`

:   Names of the Seurat images to use.

`sample_id`

:   Names of the samples to plot. Use it for multi-sample SIRUP objects. If `NULL`, the function plots all samples.

`image_scale`

:   Image scale for `SeuratObject::GetTissueCoordinates()`. If `NULL`, the function uses the value stored in the SIRUP object.

`swap_coords`

:   Swap the two Seurat coordinate axes? If `NULL`, the function uses the value stored in the SIRUP object. Give a value if `object` is a Seurat object.

`polygon_val`

:   IDs of the polygons to select from `dominance`.

`polygon_alpha`

:   Opacity of the polygon fill in the numbered map (default 0.2).

`image_alpha`

:   Opacity of the tissue image.

`pie_alpha`

:   Opacity of the pies (default 0.9).

`label_size`

:   Text size of the polygon labels and pie labels (default 3).

`pies_per_page`

:   Largest number of pie charts on one page, if `mode = "side_by_side"` (default 6). If there are more polygons, the function returns a named list with one plot for each page.

`pie_order`

:   Order of the pie charts, if `mode = "side_by_side"`: `"receptors"` (default) puts the polygon with the most receptors first, then the next, and so on. `"polygon"` keeps the order of the numbered map. Each pie keeps its map label. The function ignores this argument if `mode = "spatial_clipped"`.

`spatial_legend`

:   Show one shared fill legend for the `spatial_clipped` plots (default `FALSE`)?

`zoom`

:   Zoom to the extent of the plotted polygons (default `FALSE`)? If `FALSE`, the plot shows the full tissue image.

`combine_sample_plots`

:   Combine the plots of all samples into one patchwork (default `FALSE`)? The function uses it only for multi-sample objects. If `FALSE`, it returns a named list with one plot for each sample.

## Details

The function uses the receptor rows in the result of [`spatialCloneDominance()`](spatialCloneDominance.md). The `mode` argument sets the plot style:

- `side_by_side`: pie charts next to a numbered map of the polygons.

- `spatial_clipped`: pie charts inside the polygon boundaries on the tissue. It needs the `sf` package.

- `dominance_only`: the pie charts only, with no map.

- `stacked_bar`: one stacked bar for each polygon in one panel, with no map. Each bar stacks the `fill` levels in dominance order.

If there are multiple samples or images, the function creates separate plots for each.

## Value

A ggplot object, a patchwork object, or a named list of ggplot objects.

## See Also

[`spatialCloneDominance()`](spatialCloneDominance.md), [`plotSpatialRegionReceptors()`](plotSpatialRegionReceptors.md)

## Examples

``` R
x <- readSIRUP(system.file("extdata", "sirup_synthetic.rds", package = "SIRUP"))
dominance <- spatialCloneDominance(x)
plotSpatialPolygonPies(dominance, x)
plotSpatialPolygonPies(dominance, x, mode = "stacked_bar")
```

functions.title: Plot polygons on a tissue image
functions.summary: Plot polygons on a tissue image
functions.markdown:
# plotSpatialPolygons

## Plot polygons on a tissue image

## Description

Plot polygons on a tissue image

## Usage

``` R
plotSpatialPolygons(
  object,
  polygon = NULL,
  images = NULL,
  sample_id = NULL,
  image_scale = NULL,
  swap_coords = NULL,
  polygon_val = NULL,
  x = "x",
  y = "y",
  polygon_id = "polygon",
  polygon_alpha = 0.2,
  polygon_fill = "#0072B2",
  fill_analysis = NULL,
  fill_column = NULL,
  analysis_fill = c("#D3D3D3", "#FFFF00"),
  polygon_color = "#0072B2",
  linewidth = 0.6,
  image_alpha = 1,
  label = TRUE,
  label_by = "polygon",
  label_size = 3,
  label_color = "black",
  label_outside = FALSE,
  label_offset = 0.08,
  label_leader = TRUE,
  label_leader_color = "grey40",
  zoom = FALSE,
  combine = TRUE,
  combine_sample_plots = FALSE
)
```

## Arguments

`object`

: Seurat object or SIRUP object.

`polygon`

: Data frame of polygon vertices in order. It needs the columns set by `x` and `y`. If the column set by `polygon_id` exists, the function treats each polygon on its own. If `object` is a SIRUP object and `polygon` is `NULL`, the function uses the stored polygons.

`images`

: Names of the Seurat images to use.

`sample_id`

: Names of the samples to plot. Use it for multi-sample SIRUP objects. If `NULL`, the function plots all samples.

`image_scale`

: Image scale for `SeuratObject::GetTissueCoordinates()`. If `NULL`, the function uses the value stored in the SIRUP object.

`swap_coords`

: Swap the two Seurat coordinate axes? If `NULL`, the function uses the value stored in the SIRUP object. Give a value if `object` is a Seurat object.

`polygon_val`

: IDs of the polygons to use. If `NULL`, the function uses all polygons.

`x`

: Name of the x-coordinate column in `polygon` (default `"x"`).

`y`

: Name of the y-coordinate column in `polygon` (default `"y"`).

`polygon_id`

: Name of the column in `polygon` that groups the vertices by polygon (default `"polygon"`).

`polygon_alpha`

: Opacity of the polygon fill (default 0.2).

`polygon_fill`

: Fill color of the polygons, if no analysis is mapped (default `"#0072B2"`).

`fill_analysis`

: Name of a stored SIRUP analysis that has one row for each polygon. The function colors the polygons with it.

`fill_column`

: Name of the column that sets the fill color. If `fill_analysis` is `NULL`, the function reads the column from the polygon data. Otherwise, it reads the column from the analysis. The analysis must have a `polygon_id` or `polygon` column as the polygon key.

`analysis_fill`

: Two colors for the low and high end of the gradient for numeric analysis values (default `c("#D3D3D3", "#FFFF00")`). The function uses the Glasbey palette for other values.

`polygon_color`

: Color of the polygon outlines (default `"#0072B2"`).

`linewidth`

: Width of the polygon outlines (default 0.6).

`image_alpha`

: Opacity of the tissue image.

`label`

: Write a label at the center of each polygon (default `TRUE`)?

`label_by`

: Name of the column in the polygon data that holds the labels (default `"polygon"`).

`label_size`

: Text size of the labels (default 3).

`label_color`

: Text color of the labels (default `"black"`).

`label_outside`

: Put each label outside its polygon (default `FALSE`)? The function pushes each label away from the centroid of all plotted polygons, so that labels spread outward from a group of small polygons. The label is `label_offset` away from the polygon.

`label_offset`

: Gap between a polygon edge and its label, if `label_outside` is `TRUE` (default 0.08). The value is a fraction of the plotted coordinate range.

`label_leader`

: Draw a line from each polygon to its label, if `label_outside` is `TRUE` (default `TRUE`)?

`label_leader_color`

: Color of the leader lines (default `"grey40"`).

`zoom`

: Zoom to the extent of the polygons, not the full tissue (default `FALSE`)?

`combine`

: Combine the plots with patchwork, if possible (default `TRUE`)?

`combine_sample_plots`

: Combine the plots of all samples into one patchwork (default `FALSE`)? The function uses it only for multi-sample objects. If `FALSE`, it returns a named list with one plot for each sample.

## Details

`plotSpatialPolygons` plots polygons over the Seurat tissue image. If there are multiple samples or images, the function creates separate plots for each.

## Value

A ggplot or patchwork object. If `combine = FALSE`, a named list of ggplot objects.

## See Also

[`selectSpatialPolygons()`](selectSpatialPolygons.md), [`spatialCloneDominance()`](spatialCloneDominance.md)

## Examples

``` R
x <- readSIRUP(system.file("extdata", "sirup_synthetic.rds", package = "SIRUP"))
plotSpatialPolygons(x)
plotSpatialPolygons(x, label_outside = TRUE)
```

functions.title: Plot receptors inside polygons using the results of \code{spatialCloneDominance()}
functions.summary: Plot receptors inside polygons using the results of [`spatialCloneDominance()`](spatialCloneDominance.md)
functions.markdown:
# plotSpatialRegionReceptors

## Plot receptors inside polygons using the results of [`spatialCloneDominance()`](spatialCloneDominance.md)

## Description

Plot receptors inside polygons using the results of [`spatialCloneDominance()`](spatialCloneDominance.md)

## Usage

``` R
plotSpatialRegionReceptors(
  dominance,
  object,
  color = "clone_id",
  images = NULL,
  sample_id = NULL,
  image_scale = NULL,
  swap_coords = NULL,
  polygon_val = NULL,
  point_size = 1,
  point_alpha = 0.5,
  polygon_alpha = 0.12,
  polygon_fill = "#FFFFFF",
  polygon_color = "black",
  image_alpha = 1,
  top_n = NULL,
  other_label = "Other",
  other_color = "#D3D3D3",
  plot_other = TRUE,
  zoom = FALSE,
  combine = TRUE,
  combine_sample_plots = FALSE
)
```

## Arguments

`dominance`

:   Result of [`spatialCloneDominance()`](spatialCloneDominance.md).

`object`

:   Seurat object or SIRUP object.

`color`

:   Name of the column in `dominance$region_receptors` that sets the color of the points. If you omit it, the function uses the clone column that [`spatialCloneDominance()`](spatialCloneDominance.md) recorded (default `"clone_id"`).

`images`

:   Names of the Seurat images to use.

`sample_id`

:   Names of the samples to plot. Use it for multi-sample SIRUP objects. If `NULL`, the function plots all samples.

`image_scale`

:   Image scale for `SeuratObject::GetTissueCoordinates()`. If `NULL`, the function uses the value stored in the SIRUP object.

`swap_coords`

:   Swap the two Seurat coordinate axes? If `NULL`, the function uses the value stored in the SIRUP object. Give a value if `object` is a Seurat object.

`polygon_val`

:   IDs of the polygons to select from `dominance`.

`point_size`

:   Size of the receptor points (default 1).

`point_alpha`

:   Opacity of the receptor points (default 0.5).

`polygon_alpha`

:   Opacity of the polygon fill (default 0.12).

`polygon_fill`

:   Fill color of the polygons (default `"#FFFFFF"`).

`polygon_color`

:   Color of the polygon outlines (default `"black"`).

`image_alpha`

:   Opacity of the tissue image.

`top_n`

:   Number of the most frequent `color` levels to show. The function groups the other levels under `other_label`. If `NULL`, it shows all levels.

`other_label`

:   Label for the grouped levels (default `"Other"`).

`other_color`

:   Color of the grouped levels (default `"#D3D3D3"`).

`plot_other`

:   Plot the grouped levels (default `TRUE`)?

`zoom`

:   Zoom to the extent of the selected polygons (default `FALSE`)? If `FALSE`, the plot shows the full tissue image.

`combine`

:   Combine the plots with patchwork, if possible (default `TRUE`)?

`combine_sample_plots`

:   Combine the plots of all samples into one patchwork (default `FALSE`)? The function uses it only for multi-sample objects. If `FALSE`, it returns a named list with one plot for each sample.

## Details

`plotSpatialRegionReceptors` plots the receptors inside the polygons on the tissue image. The result of [`spatialCloneDominance()`](spatialCloneDominance.md) supplies the receptors. If there are multiple samples or images, the function creates separate plots for each.

## Value

A ggplot or patchwork object. If `combine = FALSE`, a named list of ggplot objects.

## See Also

[`spatialCloneDominance()`](spatialCloneDominance.md), [`plotSpatialPolygonPies()`](plotSpatialPolygonPies.md)

## Examples

``` R
x <- readSIRUP(system.file("extdata", "sirup_synthetic.rds", package = "SIRUP"))
dominance <- spatialCloneDominance(x)
plotSpatialRegionReceptors(dominance, x)
```

functions.summary: `polygonAbundance` runs [`alakazam::estimateAbundance()`](https://alakazam.readthedocs.io/en/stable/topics/estimateAbundance/) once on the receptors of all polygons, with the polygon as the group.
functions.markdown:
# polygonAbundance

## Estimate clonal abundance inside polygons

## Description

`polygonAbundance` runs [`alakazam::estimateAbundance()`](https://alakazam.readthedocs.io/en/stable/topics/estimateAbundance/) once on the receptors of all polygons, with the polygon as the group. alakazam then resamples every polygon to the same number of receptors, so the curves of different polygons are comparable. With `common_size = FALSE`, the function analyses each polygon alone instead.

## Usage

``` R
polygonAbundance(
  receptors,
  polygons = NULL,
  polygon_id = "polygon",
  analysis_name = NULL,
  clone = "clone_id",
  copy = NULL,
  common_size = TRUE,
  slot = NULL,
  min_n = 10,
  max_n = NULL,
  uniform = TRUE,
  ci = 0.95,
  nboot = 2000,
  cell_id = NULL,
  progress = FALSE,
  validate = TRUE
)
```

## Arguments

`receptors`

:   SIRUP object, or an AIRR-style receptor table.

`polygons`

:   Polygon table that sets the polygons to use. If `NULL`, the function takes the polygon IDs from the SIRUP object, or from the `polygon_id` values in `receptors`.

`polygon_id`

:   Name of the column that holds the primary polygon of each receptor (default `"polygon"`). For a SIRUP object, the default is `"polygon_id"`.

`analysis_name`

:   Name for the stored result in a SIRUP object (default `"polygon_abundance"`). If the object has several receptor slots, the default also ends with `⁠_⁠` and the slot name.

`clone`

:   Name of the column that holds the clone IDs (default `"clone_id"`).

`copy`

:   Name of the column that holds the copy number of each sequence (default `NULL`). If `NULL`, the function measures clone abundance as the number of sequences. Otherwise, it uses the sum of the copy numbers in each clone.

`common_size`

:   Resample all polygons to the same size (default `TRUE`)? If `FALSE`, the function analyses each polygon alone, as in earlier versions of SIRUP, and returns a list with one result for each polygon.

`slot`

:   Name of the receptor slot to use. Leave it `NULL` if the SIRUP object has one receptor table. You must give it if the object has several slots. The function ignores `slot` if you give a plain receptor table.

`min_n`

:   Smallest number of receptors that a polygon needs (default 10). The function drops a polygon with fewer receptors. With `common_size = TRUE`, the smallest polygon that stays sets the size of the resampling, so a larger `min_n` gives less noisy curves and keeps fewer polygons.

`max_n`

:   Largest number of receptors to sample from each polygon (default `NULL`). If `NULL`, the size is the size of the smallest polygon that stays.

`uniform`

:   Resample each polygon to the same number of receptors (default `TRUE`)? Passed to [`alakazam::estimateAbundance()`](https://alakazam.readthedocs.io/en/stable/topics/estimateAbundance/).

`ci`

:   Confidence interval, between 0 and 1 (default 0.95).

`nboot`

:   Number of bootstrap samples (default 2000).

`cell_id`

:   Name of the column that holds the cell IDs (default `NULL`). If `NULL`, the function assumes bulk data.

`progress`

:   Show a progress bar (default `FALSE`)?

`validate`

:   Validate the updated SIRUP object (default `TRUE`)?

## Details

The function puts the receptors of all polygons in one table and passes the polygon column to [`alakazam::estimateAbundance()`](https://alakazam.readthedocs.io/en/stable/topics/estimateAbundance/) as `group`. With `uniform = TRUE` (the default), alakazam resamples each polygon to the size of the smallest polygon that has at least `min_n` receptors. Use `max_n` to set a smaller size. The function leaves out polygons with fewer than `min_n` receptors. If no polygon has enough receptors, the function gives an error.

The result is one `AbundanceCurve` object. Its `abundance` table has one column of polygon IDs. [`alakazam::plotAbundanceCurve()`](https://alakazam.readthedocs.io/en/stable/topics/plotAbundanceCurve/) plots all polygons together. For a SIRUP object, the function stores the result as an analysis and returns the updated object.

With `common_size = FALSE`, the function runs [`alakazam::estimateAbundance()`](https://alakazam.readthedocs.io/en/stable/topics/estimateAbundance/) once for each polygon. Each polygon is then resampled to its own size, so polygons with more receptors can look more diverse. A polygon with fewer than `min_n` receptors gives `NULL`. The result is a named list with one `AbundanceCurve` for each polygon.

The arguments from `clone` to `progress` go to [`alakazam::estimateAbundance()`](https://alakazam.readthedocs.io/en/stable/topics/estimateAbundance/).

## Value

For a SIRUP object, the updated SIRUP object. Otherwise, the abundance results: one `AbundanceCurve` object, or a list with one object for each polygon if `common_size = FALSE`.

## See Also

[`polygonDiversity()`](polygonDiversity.md), [`withPolygons()`](withPolygons.md)

## Examples

``` R
x <- readSIRUP(system.file("extdata", "sirup_synthetic.rds", package = "SIRUP"))

# The example polygons have few receptors, so lower min_n.
x <- polygonAbundance(x, min_n = 2, nboot = 50)
listAnalyses(x)
```

functions.markdown:
# polygonDiversity

## Estimate clonal diversity inside polygons

## Description

`polygonDiversity` runs [`alakazam::alphaDiversity()`](https://alakazam.readthedocs.io/en/stable/topics/alphaDiversity/) once on the receptors of all polygons, with the polygon as the group. alakazam then resamples every polygon to the same number of receptors, so the diversity of different polygons is comparable. With `common_size = FALSE`, the function analyses each polygon alone instead.

## Usage

``` R
polygonDiversity(
  receptors,
  polygons = NULL,
  polygon_id = "polygon",
  analysis_name = NULL,
  clone = "clone_id",
  copy = NULL,
  common_size = TRUE,
  slot = NULL,
  min_n = 10,
  min_q = 0,
  max_q = 4,
  step_q = 0.1,
  ci = 0.95,
  ...,
  validate = TRUE
)
```

## Arguments

`receptors`

:   SIRUP object, or an AIRR-style receptor table.

`polygons`

:   Polygon table that sets the polygons to use. If `NULL`, the function takes the polygon IDs from the SIRUP object, or from the `polygon_id` values in `receptors`.

`polygon_id`

:   Name of the column that holds the primary polygon of each receptor (default `"polygon"`). For a SIRUP object, the default is `"polygon_id"`.

`analysis_name`

:   Name for the stored result in a SIRUP object (default `"polygon_diversity"`). If the object has several receptor slots, the default also ends with `⁠_⁠` and the slot name.

`clone`

:   Name of the column that holds the clone IDs (default `"clone_id"`).

`copy`

:   Name of the column that holds the copy number of each sequence (default `NULL`). If `NULL`, the function measures clone abundance as the number of sequences. Otherwise, it uses the sum of the copy numbers in each clone.

`common_size`

:   Resample all polygons to the same size (default `TRUE`)? If `FALSE`, the function analyses each polygon alone, as in earlier versions of SIRUP, and returns a list with one result for each polygon.

`slot`

:   Name of the receptor slot to use. Leave it `NULL` if the SIRUP object has one receptor table. You must give it if the object has several slots. The function ignores `slot` if you give a plain receptor table.

`min_n`

:   Smallest number of receptors that a polygon needs (default 10). The function drops a polygon with fewer receptors. With `common_size = TRUE`, the smallest polygon that stays sets the size of the resampling, so a larger `min_n` gives less noisy estimates and keeps fewer polygons.

`min_q`

:   Smallest diversity order q (default 0).

`max_q`

:   Largest diversity order q (default 4).

`step_q`

:   Step between the values of q (default 0.1).

`ci`

:   Confidence interval, between 0 and 1 (default 0.95).

`...`

:   Other arguments for [`alakazam::alphaDiversity()`](https://alakazam.readthedocs.io/en/stable/topics/alphaDiversity/), such as `nboot`, `max_n` and `uniform`. You cannot give `group`, because the function uses the polygon as the group.

`validate`

:   Validate the updated SIRUP object (default `TRUE`)?

## Details

The function puts the receptors of all polygons in one table and passes the polygon column to [`alakazam::alphaDiversity()`](https://alakazam.readthedocs.io/en/stable/topics/alphaDiversity/) as `group`. alakazam resamples each polygon to the size of the smallest polygon that has at least `min_n` receptors. Use `max_n` (through `...`) to set a smaller size. The function leaves out polygons with fewer than `min_n` receptors. If no polygon has enough receptors, the function gives an error.

The result is one `DiversityCurve` object. Its `diversity` table has one column of polygon IDs. [`alakazam::plotDiversityCurve()`](https://alakazam.readthedocs.io/en/stable/topics/plotDiversityCurve/) plots all polygons together. For a SIRUP object, the function stores the result as an analysis and returns the updated object.

With `common_size = FALSE`, the function runs [`alakazam::alphaDiversity()`](https://alakazam.readthedocs.io/en/stable/topics/alphaDiversity/) once for each polygon. Each polygon is then resampled to its own size, so polygons with more receptors can look more diverse. A polygon with fewer than `min_n` receptors gives `NULL`. The result is a named list with one `DiversityCurve` for each polygon.

The arguments from `clone` to `...` go to [`alakazam::alphaDiversity()`](https://alakazam.readthedocs.io/en/stable/topics/alphaDiversity/).

## Value

For a SIRUP object, the updated SIRUP object. Otherwise, the diversity results: one `DiversityCurve` object, or a list with one object for each polygon if `common_size = FALSE`.

## See Also

[`summarizePolygonDiversity()`](summarizePolygonDiversity.md), [`polygonAbundance()`](polygonAbundance.md)

## Examples

``` R
x <- readSIRUP(system.file("extdata", "sirup_synthetic.rds", package = "SIRUP"))
x <- polygonDiversity(x, min_n = 2, max_q = 2, step_q = 1)
listAnalyses(x)
```

# polygonReceptorSummary

## Summarize columns in receptors data inside polygons

## Description

`polygonReceptorSummary` makes one summary row for each polygon.

## Usage

``` R
polygonReceptorSummary(
  object,
  polygons = NULL,
  spatial_id = NULL,
  polygon_id = "polygon",
  clone = "clone_id",
  weight = NULL,
  summary_columns = NULL,
  summary_operations = NULL,
  include_total_spots = FALSE,
  analysis_name = NULL,
  slot = NULL,
  validate = TRUE
)
```

## Arguments

`object`

:   SIRUP object, or an AIRR-style receptor table.

`polygons`

:   Polygon table that sets the order of the output polygons. If `NULL`, the function takes the polygon IDs from the SIRUP object, or from the `polygon_id` values in `object`.

`spatial_id`

:   Name of the column that holds the spatial IDs. If `NULL`, the function uses the stored field of a SIRUP object, or looks for a standard spatial ID column in the receptor table.

`polygon_id`

:   Name of the column that holds the primary polygon of each receptor (default `"polygon"`).

`clone`

:   Name of the column that holds the clone IDs (default `"clone_id"`). The function uses it for `n_clones` and `top_clone_fraction`. If the column does not exist, the function leaves out these two summaries.

`weight`

:   Name of a numeric column that holds the receptor weights. If you give it, `n_receptors`, `top_clone_fraction`, and the numeric custom summaries use the weights.

`summary_columns`

:   Names of the receptor columns to summarize.

`summary_operations`

:   Operations for `summary_columns`. Give one operation, or one for each column. The operations are `count`, `sum`, `mean`, `median`, `variance`, `var`, `sd`, `min`, `max`, `any`, `all`, and `cat`.

`include_total_spots`

:   Add `n_total_spatial_ids` (default `FALSE`)? This column holds the number of all spots in each polygon, including spots with no receptor rows. It works only for SIRUP objects.

`analysis_name`

:   Name for the stored summary in a SIRUP object (default `"polygon_receptor_summary"`). If the object has several receptor slots, the default also ends with `⁠_⁠` and the slot name.

`slot`

:   Name of the receptor slot to use. Leave it `NULL` if the SIRUP object has one receptor table. You must give it if the object has several slots. The function ignores `slot` if you give a plain receptor table.

`validate`

:   Validate the updated SIRUP object (default `TRUE`)?

## Details

The input can be a SIRUP object or a receptor table that already has polygon columns. For a SIRUP object, the function stores the summary as an analysis and returns the updated object. For a receptor table, it returns the summary tibble.

## Value

For a SIRUP object, the updated SIRUP object. Otherwise, a summary tibble.

## See Also

[`assignReceptorPolygons()`](assignReceptorPolygons.md), [`polygonDiversity()`](polygonDiversity.md)

## Examples

``` R
x <- readSIRUP(system.file("extdata", "sirup_synthetic.rds", package = "SIRUP"))
x <- polygonReceptorSummary(x)
getAnalysis(x, "polygon_receptor_summary")
```

functions.title: Process one spatial sample from reads to an AIRR table
functions.summary: `processSpatialSample`processes demultiplexed reads for one sample and one receptor group (`ig` or `tr`).
functions.markdown:
# processSpatialSample

## Process one spatial sample from reads to an AIRR table

## Description

`processSpatialSample`processes demultiplexed reads for one sample and one receptor group (`ig` or `tr`). It outputs an AIRR table of filtered consensus sequences, with the V(D)J genes assigned and IMGT-gaps added.

## Usage

``` R
processSpatialSample(
  input,
  output_dir = NULL,
  receptor = c("ig", "tr"),
  organism = "human",
  input_type = c("auto", "raw_reads", "airr", "spatial_fasta"),
  filter_args = list(),
  invalid_spatial_ids = c("abort", "drop"),
  fasta_sequence_col = "sequence_alignment",
  sample_name = NULL,
  identity = 0.975,
  consensus_freq = 0.51,
  germline_glob = NULL,
  igblast_refs = NULL,
  imgt_dir = NULL,
  igblast_base = "~/software/igblast",
  muscle_exec = "~/software/muscle3.8.31_i86linux64",
  nproc = 8,
  cluster_field = "barcode",
  delimiters = c("|", "=", ","),
  parse_fields = c(cluster_field, "cluster"),
  parse_key = paste0(cluster_field, "_cluster"),
  parse_act = "set",
  consensus_min_count = 1,
  umi_support = FALSE,
  umi_weight = TRUE,
  umi_field = "umi",
  umi_identity = 0.95,
  min_umi_support = 2,
  consensus_copy_fields = NULL,
  consensus_copy_action = "majority",
  consensus_max_error = 0.1,
  consensus_max_gap = 0.3,
  skip_existing = FALSE,
  align_log = NULL,
  consensus_log = NULL
)
```

## Arguments

`input`

:   Raw reads (FASTA or FASTQ, optionally gzipped), the path of an AIRR TSV, an AIRR data frame, or a FASTA that is ready for pRESTO.

`output_dir`

:   Directory for all outputs. The default is the directory of the input file. You must give it if `input` is a data frame.

`receptor`

:   `"ig"` for BCR loci or `"tr"` for TCR loci.

`organism`

:   Organism of the sample (default `"human"`).

`input_type`

:   How to treat `input`: `"auto"` (default), `"raw_reads"`, `"airr"`, or `"spatial_fasta"`. With `"auto"`, the function finds the type from the class of the object and the file extension. A FASTA or FASTQ path becomes `"raw_reads"`. Use `"spatial_fasta"` to send a FASTA that is ready for pRESTO straight to the consensus workflow. For a new rrad FASTA, use `"auto"` or `"raw_reads"`, because `"spatial_fasta"` skips the first annotation of V(D)J genes and the filtering of the reads.

`filter_args`

:   Named list that changes arguments of [`filterAirr()`](filterAirr.md). The pipeline defaults are `complete_vdj = TRUE`, `min_consensus_count = NULL`, `spatial_id = "barcode"`, `add_spatial_sequence_id = TRUE`, and `spatial_id_key = cluster_field`. A `NULL` value turns off an optional filter (`locus_val`, `min_consensus_count`, `max_opening_gap`, or `spatial_id`). The other arguments do not accept `NULL`.

`invalid_spatial_ids`

:   What to do with filtered rows whose spatial barcode is missing or holds a delimiter: `"abort"` (default) stops with a count, and `"drop"` removes the rows with a warning.

`fasta_sequence_col`

:   Name of the AIRR column to write to the spatial FASTA (default `"sequence_alignment"`, the aligned V(D)J region). This keeps extra read sequence out of the clustering and consensus steps. Use `"sequence"` to write the full read.

`sample_name`

:   Stem of the intermediate file names. The default is the input file name without the extension, or `"sample"` for a data frame.

`identity`

:   Identity threshold for the clusters, passed to `ClusterSets.py` (default 0.975).

`consensus_freq`

:   Frequency threshold for the consensus, passed to `BuildConsensus.py` (default 0.51).

`germline_glob`

:   Pattern of the germline files, such as `⁠<imgt_dir>/human/vdj/imgt_human_*.fasta⁠`. The function uses it only to find `imgt_dir` if `imgt_dir` is `NULL`.

`igblast_refs`

:   Folder with the IgBLAST `⁠database/⁠` and `⁠fasta/⁠` folders (the `refs` argument of `airrblast::assignGenes()`). If `NULL`, the function uses `igblast_base`.

`imgt_dir`

:   IMGT folder with the gapped germlines, at `⁠<imgt_dir>/<organism>/vdj⁠` (the `gapdb` argument of `airrblast::addGaps()`). If `NULL`, the function finds it from `germline_glob`, which must point into a `⁠<organism>/vdj⁠` folder.

`igblast_base`

:   IgBLAST installation folder (default `"~/software/igblast"`). The function passes it to `airrblast::assignGenes()` as `igblast`. The folder must hold `bin/igblastn`.

`muscle_exec`

:   Path of the MUSCLE program, passed to `AlignSets.py --exec` (default `"~/software/muscle3.8.31_i86linux64"`).

`nproc`

:   Number of processors for the IgBLAST step on raw reads, for pRESTO, and for the gene assignment (default 8).

`cluster_field`

:   FASTA header field for the clustering within a spot (default `"barcode"`, the parsed rrad `BARCODE` field). The pipeline writes the headers with this field name. Change it for other spatial ID fields, such as `barcode_8um`.

`delimiters`

:   Character vector of the pRESTO delimiters, passed after `--delim` (default `c("|", "=", ",")`).

`parse_fields`

:   Header fields for `⁠ParseHeaders.py merge -f⁠` (default `c(cluster_field, "cluster")`).

`parse_key`

:   Name of the header field that `⁠ParseHeaders.py merge -k⁠` makes (default `paste0(cluster_field, "_cluster")`).

`parse_act`

:   Action for `⁠ParseHeaders.py merge --act⁠` (default `"set"`). With `"set"`, the function joins the spatial ID and the cluster ID with a comma, so that you can recover the spatial ID from the consensus header. With `"cat"`, it joins them with no separator, so that you cannot recover the spatial ID of a barcode that has a variable length. Both give the same groups, so use `"set"`.

`consensus_min_count`

:   Smallest number of sequences for a consensus, passed to `BuildConsensus.py -n` (default 1). Use at least 2 for data that do not have single-cell resolution. This value decides which groups the function writes. It does not change the consensus of a group that passes. So you can run with `1` and filter to a higher value later with `filterAirr(min_consensus_count = )`. `BuildConsensus.py -q` is fixed at 20 and has no effect here, because the pipeline input is FASTA and has no base qualities.

`umi_support`

:   Group the reads by spatial barcode and UMI before the barcode step (default `FALSE`)? Reads of one molecule that differ by a sequencing error end up in different clusters at `identity = 1.0`, and the function then drops them as singletons. This stage first joins them at `umi_identity`, so that they support each other. Each barcode-UMI cluster gives one consensus. The consensus carries `cc_bc_umi` (the number of reads in the cluster, counted before the productive subset) and `n_productive_reads` (the number of reads that the consensus uses). The function discards a cluster that has no such reads. The barcode step then runs with `⁠BuildConsensus -n 1⁠` and sums both fields, and `min_umi_support` replaces the read minimum. With `umi_weight = TRUE`, the function writes each consensus once for each productive read, so that one read is one vote in the barcode consensus. A short read from one molecule then cannot trim the consensus of many full-length reads. For this reason, `consensus_count` counts reads and not molecules. The option needs an AIRR table with the columns `umi` and `productive`.

`umi_weight`

:   Write each molecule consensus once for each productive read (default `TRUE`)? The function uses it only with `umi_support`. If `FALSE`, it writes each molecule once, so that one UMI cluster is one vote.

`umi_field`

:   Name of the column that holds the UMI (default `"umi"`). The function uses it only with `umi_support`.

`umi_identity`

:   Identity threshold for the barcode-UMI clusters (default 0.95). It is lower than `identity` on purpose, so that reads of one molecule with errors form one group.

`min_umi_support`

:   Smallest summed `cc_bc_umi` that a barcode consensus needs (default 2). The function applies it after the gene assignment. It writes a filtered copy next to `db_pass`, so that you can change the threshold without a new run of the pipeline.

`consensus_copy_fields`

:   Header fields for `BuildConsensus.py --cf`. With `umi_support`, the function adds `CC_BC_UMI` and `N_PRODUCTIVE_READS` at the start of the list and sums them.

`consensus_copy_action`

:   Action for `BuildConsensus.py --act`, if you give `consensus_copy_fields` (default `"majority"`).

`consensus_max_error`

:   Largest error rate, passed to `BuildConsensus.py --maxerror` (default 0.1).

`consensus_max_gap`

:   Largest gap fraction, passed to `BuildConsensus.py --maxgap` (default 0.3).

`skip_existing`

:   Skip a pipeline command if its output already exists and is not empty (default `FALSE`)? Use it to restart an interrupted run. You can also use it to reuse one clustering and alignment pass for several `consensus_freq` values, because those steps depend only on `identity`.

`align_log`

:   Path of a log file for `AlignSets.py --log`.

`consensus_log`

:   Path of a log file for `BuildConsensus.py --log`.

## Details

The function calls external programs: IgBLAST, pRESTO, vsearch, and MUSCLE. It prints each command before it runs it. The function runs all commands with `system2()` and no shell. A non-zero exit status stops the function, and the error message shows the command that failed. The final output is the `db_pass` AIRR TSV, which is in the returned list of paths.

The `input` can be one of these:

- Raw reads: a FASTA or FASTQ file, optionally gzipped, from RRAD (or RAD). Export the rrad FASTA with `to_fasta = TRUE` and `header_format = "presto"`, so that the barcode and UMI tags stay in the IgBLAST identifier. The function first annotates the reads with [`runIgblast()`](runIgblast.md) (which calls `airrblast::assignGenes()`). This step needs `igblast_base` and `igblast_refs`.

- An AIRR table: a `.tsv` path or a data frame. The function skips the IgBLAST step. A data frame needs `output_dir`.

- A FASTA that is ready for pRESTO (`input_type = "spatial_fasta"`). The function skips the IgBLAST and filter steps, and starts with the consensus workflow.

For raw reads and AIRR tables, the function first does these steps:

1.  It splits the rrad tags `⁠|BARCODE=...|UMI=...⁠` (or the legacy colon tags) out of `sequence_id` with [`parseRadSequenceIds()`](parseRadSequenceIds.md).

2.  It filters sequences with [`filterAirr()`](filterAirr.md). The pipeline defaults are `complete_vdj = TRUE`, `spatial_id = "barcode"`, and a combined header ID with the key `cluster_field`. Change them with `filter_args`.

3.  It writes the raw and the filtered AIRR tables to `output_dir`, so that you can inspect them.

4.  It writes the filtered sequences to a spatial FASTA file. The headers of the file hold the spatial ID.

The spatial FASTA then goes through a number of Immcantation functions:

1.  `⁠ClusterSets.py set⁠` groups the reads within each spatial ID. It uses `cluster_field`, the identity threshold `identity`, and vsearch.

2.  `⁠ParseHeaders.py merge⁠` writes a new header field, `parse_key`. The field combines the spatial ID and the cluster ID (`parse_fields`) with the action `parse_act`. `delimiters` sets the delimiters of the FASTA header.

3.  `⁠AlignSets.py muscle⁠` aligns the reads within each `parse_key` group. `muscle_exec` is the path of the MUSCLE program (<https://github.com/rcedgar/muscle>). The function can write a log to `align_log`.

4.  `BuildConsensus.py` makes a consensus sequence for each `parse_key` group. `consensus_min_count` is the smallest number of sequences that give a valid consensus. `consensus_freq` is the fraction of occurrences below which the function assigns an ambiguous character. The function can write a log to `consensus_log`. To copy more header fields to the consensus file, give their names in `consensus_copy_fields` and the way to copy them in `consensus_copy_action` (`majority`, `first`, `last`, or `all`).

5.  `airrblast::assignGenes()` assigns the V(D)J genes with IgBLAST. It replaces `AssignGenes.py`. `receptor` is `ig` (BCR) or `tr` (TCR). `organism` is the species (human, mouse, or rhesus_monkey). `igblast_base` is the IgBLAST installation, which must hold `bin/igblastn`. `igblast_refs` is the folder with the IgBLAST `⁠database/⁠` and `⁠fasta/⁠` folders.

6.  `airrblast::addGaps()` adds the IMGT-gapped sequences from the germlines in `imgt_dir`. SIRUP then reads the pRESTO header fields into columns, as `MakeDb.py --extended` did. It keeps the sequences that have a V call, a J call, a productive flag, an aligned sequence, and a junction. The result is the `db_pass` table.

## Value

A named list, invisibly. It holds `raw_airr`, `filtered_airr`, `spatial_fasta`, `n_raw`, and `n_filtered`, which are `NULL` for the steps that did not run. It also holds the output paths of pRESTO and IgBLAST. `db_pass` is the final AIRR TSV. With `umi_support`, `db_pass_umi` is the same table, filtered to `min_umi_support`.

## See Also

[`processSpatialSamples()`](processSpatialSamples.md), [`runIgblast()`](runIgblast.md), [`filterAirr()`](filterAirr.md), [`parseRadSequenceIds()`](parseRadSequenceIds.md)

## Examples

``` R
## Not run: 
# This example needs IgBLAST, pRESTO, vsearch, and MUSCLE. See
# vignette("processing", package = "SIRUP").
result <- processSpatialSample(
  "sample1_reads.fasta.gz",
  output_dir = "sample1_output",
  receptor = "ig",
  organism = "human",
  igblast_base = "~/software/igblast",
  imgt_dir = "~/share/germlines/imgt",
  muscle_exec = "~/software/muscle",
  nproc = 8
)
bcrs <- airr::read_rearrangement(result$db_pass)

## End(Not run)
```

# processSpatialSamples

## Process several spatial samples

## Description

`processSpatialSamples` runs [`processSpatialSample()`](processSpatialSample.md) on each input in turn.

``` R
processSpatialSamples(inputs, output_dirs = NULL, sample_names = NULL, ...)
```

## Arguments

:   List or character vector of inputs, one for each sample. Each input goes to [`processSpatialSample()`](processSpatialSample.md). It can be a reads file, the path of an AIRR TSV, or an AIRR data frame.

:   Vector of output directories, one for each input. If `NULL`, each sample uses the default of [`processSpatialSample()`](processSpatialSample.md).

`sample_names`

:   Vector of sample names, one for each input. If `NULL`, the function uses the file name of each input, or `⁠sample_<i>⁠` for a data frame.

`...`

:   Other arguments for [`processSpatialSample()`](processSpatialSample.md).

## Value

A list with one list of output paths for each sample, invisibly.

## See Also

[`processSpatialSample()`](processSpatialSample.md)

## Examples

``` R
## Not run: 
# This example needs IgBLAST, pRESTO, vsearch, and MUSCLE.
results <- processSpatialSamples(
  c("sample1_reads.fasta.gz", "sample2_reads.fasta.gz"),
  output_dirs = c("sample1_output", "sample2_output"),

)

```

# readSpatialIdMapping

## Read a spatial ID mapping file

## Description

`readSpatialIdMapping` reads a table that maps spatial IDs to other values, such as tissue positions. The file can be CSV, TSV, or parquet.

``` R
readSpatialIdMapping(path)
```

:   Path of the mapping file.

The function chooses the format from the file extension. A parquet file needs the `arrow` package.

A data frame.

positions <- data.frame(
